title: Simulating Natural Response of RC Circuits Using PySpice

questions.q: What is the natural response of an RC circuit?
questions.a: It is the transient discharge of energy stored in the capacitor through connected resistors when no independent voltage or current source drives the RC network.

questions.q: Why does Experiment 4 include two switches S1 and S2?
questions.a: S1 connects V1 to charge the capacitor prior to switchingtime (50 ms), and at 50 ms S1 opens while S2 closes to isolate V1 and discharge C1 purely through R2, R3, and R4.

questions.q: How is the discharge time constant calculated in Experiment 4?
questions.a: First find R_eq = R2 + (R3 || R4) = 32 kΩ + (240k * 60k)/(240k + 60k) = 32 kΩ + 48 kΩ = 80 kΩ. Then tau = R_eq * C1 = 80 kΩ * 0.5 µF = 40 ms.

questions.q: What is the purpose of `Rtesta` and `Rtestb` in Experiment 4?
questions.a: They provide a DC path to ground and load termination for the control pulse voltage sources `Vpulse2` and `Vpulse3` at nodes `posa` and `posb`.

questions.q: How do you set the initial capacitor voltage in PySpice before running transient analysis?
How is the switch model declared in PySpice?
How are R2, R3, and R4 connected in the discharge network of Experiment 4?
questions.a: R3 and R4 are in parallel between Node 2 and GND, and R2 is in series between Switch S2 (Node 'b') and Node 2.

questions.q: What is the capacitor voltage at 1 time constant after switching (t = 50 ms + 40 ms = 90 ms)?
What happens if a student asks for Capacitor Voltage plot and the script only runs `simulator.transient()` without `matplotlib`?
questions.a: No waveform is displayed or saved; the script must extract `analysis['output']`, plot it against `analysis.time`, label axes, and call `plt.show()` / `plt.savefig()`.

questions.q: What happens to the discharge curve if C1 is doubled from 0.5 µF to 1.0 µF?
questions.a: The discharge time constant tau doubles from 40 ms to 80 ms, so the capacitor discharges twice as slowly.
